theme: Refreshing memory without stalling the reads
title: Weak Rows, Strong Rows: Retention-Binned DRAM Refresh Scheduling
strategies: round-robin refresh every row every slot, period = bank row count, ignoring retention and access trace entirely (trivial baseline)
uniform worst-case refresh: use each bank's single weakest row's retention for every row in that bank, earliest-slot round-robin, ignoring the access trace (greedy, the obvious 'safe' recipe)

per-row retention binning: refresh each row at its own true cadence (weak often, strong rarely, some strong rows never within the horizon) and hand cold-load residues to the most frequent rows first (strong)
joint cross-row phase optimisation / exact minimum-stall assignment under the capacity and deadline constraints (open ceiling, uncovered -- the joint assignment is a hard combinatorial problem)
